channel.title: Standalone News — Original Explainers
channel.description: Source-linked, AI-assisted explainers based on official announcements

item.title: Department of Justice Secures Denaturalization of Two Individuals
item.description: The Department of Justice reported the removal of U.S. citizenship from two people following federal court orders. Officials stated the individuals obtained citizenship by withholding information regarding past illegal actions during their application processes. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: American Citizen Pleads Guilty to Multi-Year Military Identity Theft Scheme
item.description: A U.S. citizen has entered a guilty plea for operating an international identity theft and fraud scheme that compromised the bank accounts and benefits of thousands of military-affiliated individuals from overseas. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Department of Justice and EEOC Secure Joint Settlement With Delivery Service
item.description: The Department of Justice and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission announced a joint settlement with Maplebear Inc., doing business as Instacart, addressing allegations of discrimination against workers based on citizenship status and national origin. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Justice Department and Education Department Reach Settlement With UNC to Resolve Discrimination Investigations
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice and the Department of Education announced a voluntary settlement agreement with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill to address concerns regarding antisemitism and race discrimination under federal civil rights laws. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Department of Justice Secures Settlement From Mortgage Servicer Over Servicemembers Civil Relief Act Violations
item.description: The Department of Justice announced a settlement requiring a mortgage servicer to pay financial penalties and compensation to resolve allegations of violating federal laws protecting military members, including failing to apply required interest rate caps and engaging in retaliatory actions. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Somerset Lifesciences Agrees to Four Million Dollar Settlement Over Medicare Claims
item.description: Somerset Lifesciences Inc. reached an agreement with the Department of Justice to pay four million dollars to resolve claims involving Medicare Part D payments for its generic drug Olopatadine after a brand name equivalent transitioned to over-the-counter status. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Kansas Health Care Software Company Owner Sentenced to Prison for Fraud Scheme
item.description: The Department of Justice announced that a Kansas chief executive officer was sentenced to prison for operating an internet platform that produced fraudulent doctors’ orders and prescriptions, resulting in billings of over $1 billion to Medicare and other federal health benefit programs. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Justice Department Challenges St. Paul and Portland Local Ordinances Concerning Federal Officers
item.description: The Department of Justice announced the filing of lawsuits against the cities of St. Paul and Portland, contesting local ordinances that restrict federal law enforcement officers from wearing masks and mandate specific identification protocols. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Justice Department and FTC File Complaint Against California Ticket Broker Over BOTS Act Violations
item.description: The Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission filed a legal complaint against a California corporation and three of its executives, alleging unlawful acquisition and resale of event tickets using prohibited methods. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: New Self-Disclosure Protocol Streamlines Reporting for Health Care Fraud
item.description: The Department of Justice and the Department of Health and Human Services announced a streamlined self-disclosure policy allowing companies to report potential criminal health care conduct exclusively to the Justice Department to receive benefits from both agencies. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Justice Department Secures Settlement With Lexington Addressing Law Enforcement Practices
item.description: The Justice Department announced a settlement with the City of Lexington, Mississippi, to address civil rights violations identified in a previous findings report concerning the local police department. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Justice and Labor Departments Reach Enforcement Agreement with Cloudera Over PERM Recruitment Allegations
item.description: The Department of Justice and the Department of Labor announced an enforcement resolution with Cloudera Inc. addressing allegations of discrimination against U.S. workers during PERM recruitment. The resolution includes a debarment, a back-pay fund, civil penalties, and compliance measures. Source: Department of Justice

item.title: Federal Reserve Ends Enforcement Actions for Kansas Financial Institutions
item.description: The Federal Reserve concluded previous regulatory orders involving a bank holding company and its subsidiary bank in Kansas, ending multiple cease and desist directives and a corrective action directive. Source: Federal Reserve

item.title: DEA Revokes Registrations Held by Vladimir Romaniv, P.A. Following Default Determination
item.description: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order revoking specific DEA registrations held by Vladimir Romaniv, P.A., after determining the registrant was in default for failing to request a hearing and lacked the necessary state authority to handle controlled substances. Source: Federal Register · DEA

item.title: Federal Reserve Approves Isabella Bank Corporation Acquisition and Merger Application
item.description: The Federal Reserve Board approved an application by Isabella Bank Corporation to acquire Grand River Commerce, Inc. and its subsidiary. The approval also covers the subsequent bank merger and branch operations. Source: Federal Reserve

item.title: Federal Reserve Board Publishes Results of the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances
item.description: The Federal Reserve released findings from the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, offering details on assets, borrowing, and banking habits. Alongside the data, the agency published a summary report tracking shifts in income, net worth, and debt. Source: Federal Reserve

item.title: DEA Revokes Exempt Status for Inactive Butalbital Prescription Products
item.description: The Drug Enforcement Administration is revoking the exempted status for specific nonnarcotic prescription products listed on its Table of Exempted Prescription Products whose National Drug Codes are inactive because the items are no longer available or the originating company no longer exists. Source: Federal Register · DEA

item.title: Drug Enforcement Administration Revokes Registration of Montana Practitioner
item.description: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order revoking the certificate of registration held by Alexandra R. Lovec, an advanced practice registered nurse located in Ekalaka, Montana, following allegations of issuing prescriptions outside the usual course of professional practice. Source: Federal Register · DEA

item.title: Federal Reserve Finalizes Updates to Stress Test Transparency and Capital Requirements
item.description: The Federal Reserve has finalized two rules aimed at increasing transparency and reducing volatility in capital requirements for large banks. These changes include new public input processes for stress test scenarios and a revised method for calculating capital buffers, while a separate proposal seeks feedback on modeling fee income. Source: Federal Reserve
